**Current head: `11739c7f8f59455b4dc480294cab4d79f7933cb9`; tree: `43e65ee91a90ff70b70cc69d0b517b8367a2585f`.** This is a normal successor of `eef0c6d8c832ce994db1019eb5e7d6a41800b8ef`. The complete PR now changes two files: the reviewed browser observer and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

The previous exact-head [run 44831668852](https://github.com/djshellshoxxx/circula/actions/runs/44831668852) completed **six successful jobs, one failed Linux job and one conditional native-matrix placeholder skipped**. Browser job `136617856750` passed **all 597 cases**, including all four loading cases. Linux job `136617856302` failed at the service package's **20-minute deadline** (`1200.102s`); QA001 had run for 23 seconds. Its complete log has no assertion-failure or race marker; it remains a failed qualification.

The preserved successful full-race log records the service package passing in **1294.982 seconds**. The new workflow commit gives Linux packages **30 minutes** and the Linux job **45 minutes**. Every test, race flag, property seed, fuzz budget, matrix, action pin, artifact and reporting step remains. Independent source review cleared the exact patch; a semantic YAML comparison proved only these two settings changed. Whitespace, action-pin and repository-hygiene checks passed. Local reviewed commit `a4becfda0f10d5fa3790bf0ee4aeff6552dfeca1` has the exact published tree.

**Fresh provider qualification is pending on the current head.** Keep draft until all seven applicable jobs pass. After normal integration into #127, its new head must pass all nine Core and three native-reader jobs before main merge. Older successes and skipped jobs do not satisfy that gate.

Earlier source-specific records follow; their one-file scope and pending browser statements describe previous heads only.

---

## Independent review completed — 2026-11-20

Reviewed head: `eef0c6d8c832ce994db1019eb5e7d6a41800b8ef`, tree `029e5fdda2d03347389397576ec08701ae04cec2`, parent `bea5de25cf76b66d87689034e2529f9b40c6dff6`. This PR still changes only `e2e/tests/loading.spec.js`.

Independent source review and separate test engineering found no blocking issue in the complete three-path correction from `be9a5731bc93dcbf7b57301a8d2538a13af360bd`. The application sets real catalogue-backed DOM/ARIA feedback before native navigation; later cancellation cleanup and native submission behavior remain. The observer reads that actual state after the production listener and transports it through a uniquely marked console event. Request payload, focus, enabled-control, destination and reset assertions remain intact.

Exact repair-source Node helpers: **16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. The isolated negative control uses the unchanged current helpers with the exact old production script: **15 passed, one expected failure**, exclusively in the new synchronous-feedback regression. That mixed-source control is not a candidate failure. Syntax and whitespace checks pass. Playwright discovers **597 tests in 20 files**, including all four loading cases; discovery contributes **zero browser executions**. The local environment's earlier Chromium socket failure was not bypassed.

The [current repair CI](https://github.com/djshellshoxxx/circula/actions/runs/44831668852) is still qualifying this exact head. Keep draft until its applicable jobs pass. After guarded integration into PR #127, the resulting Core head requires its own nine Core jobs and three native reader jobs before main merge. The event snapshot establishes DOM/ARIA state during activation; manual rendered-pixel and assistive-technology acceptance remain separate.

Earlier observation below is preserved; its pending independent-review statement is superseded by this review.

---

## Scoped Core #127 Playwright loading harness repair

Parent of this commit is the exact current Core PR #127 head `bea5de25cf76b66d87689034e2529f9b40c6dff6`. This is a dedicated review branch; **do not merge into Core #127 before independent review and exact-head CI qualification**.

### Observed failure
- [Core run 44815660965 / browser job 136563225100](https://github.com/djshellshoxxx/circula/actions/runs/44815660965): 595/597 Playwright checks passed. Two `loading.spec.js` checks timed out in `readLoadingState(outgoing)` while a native document response was deliberately held.
- Read the complete failure log and downloaded the four-file `e2e-test-results` artifact. The failing assertion uses `JSHandle.evaluate` after the navigation request starts. A held document navigation can suspend such evaluations, so the assertion does not resolve. Browser screenshot/error context are post-release and do not prove the pending document's loading state.
- Production loading code and Node loading regression assertions were inspected. No policy or production defect is asserted by this evidence.

### Change
Replace post-navigation handle evaluation with an event-task snapshot taken synchronously by an observation-only listener installed on the outgoing document **after** the production listener. A unique console marker transports the snapshot through Playwright's existing console event channel without waiting for the pending document's execution context. Continue asserting the same loading text, status role, aria-busy state, focus preservation, control enablement, URL, form POST payload, and idle state after navigation. Route gates still hold the real GET and POST. No app source, CI workflow, assertions, or security controls changed.

### Qualification required
- Source syntax compiled via the JavaScript engine; exact diff verified as **one commit, one test file, 32 additions/25 deletions, zero behind**.
- Independent review of observer ordering, event filtering, handle semantics, and failure cleanup is **not yet complete**.
- Native browser execution of both corrected tests **not yet observed**. All 9 shared Core checks and 3 native reader checks must succeed on the eventual new **Core PR #127 head**; tests on this repair PR alone do not qualify the Core target.
- Keep #127 draft, preserve original failing CI logs and all existing branches until verified and normally integrated.

Parent `bea5de25cf76b66d87689034e2529f9b40c6dff6`; repair `eef0c6d8c832ce994db1019eb5e7d6a41800b8ef`. No release, deployment, branch deletion, history rewrite or feature activation.

Draft documentation handoff only; no merge or release approval is requested.

data.title: SEC-026: velocity and reciprocal-trade activity signals for administrators and reviewers
data.body:
**Stacked on #85 (GOV-021).** GOV-021 takes migration 0019, so this PR renumbers its migration to `0020_activity_signals.sql`. Retarget it to `main` once #85 merges. Implementation note: `docs/audit/consolidation-completion-2026-11/SEC-026.md`.

Implements core requirement SEC-026 (P1, not built before). Trades are never blocked.

**Signal rules**
- **Velocity:** a member's proposals within a window that ends at the new proposal.
- **Reciprocal:** completed trades between one pair of members, with at least one in each direction, within a window that ends at the completion.

**Deduplication and failure handling**
- At most one signal per network, kind, member (or pair) and UTC-aligned window period.
- A unique index plus `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` prevents duplicates; there is no check-then-insert.
- Evaluation runs inside a savepoint at the end of the existing write unit. If it fails, only the signal is rolled back and the trade still commits. The failure is logged after commit with only the network ID and the signal kind.

**Visibility**
- Readable only by administrators and reviewers of the same network, using the current role, break-glass and MFA checks.
- HTML page at `/n/{slug}/review/activity-signals`; `GET /api/v1/activity-signals` with a signed cursor. OpenAPI and the route table are updated.
- Each new signal sends an audit event with no member subjects, plus an anonymous inbox notice to every eligible administrator and reviewer except those it names. This covers more than 500 members via the shared `eachActiveMember` helper.

**Configuration:** five network policy fields, changed through `UpdatePolicy`. Changes are bounded, audited, prospective and announced to administrators and reviewers. Provisional defaults (owner to confirm): enabled; more than 20 proposals in 60 min; more than 10 two-way completed trades in 30 days.

**Schema:** migration 0020 adds the append-only `activity_signals` table, with CHECK constraints, composite foreign keys, the unique index and update/delete/REPLACE guards. Existing rows are unchanged.

**Acceptance tests** (26 `TestSEC026*` tests in total):

| Criterion | Tests |
|---|---|
| One signal per window, injected clock | `TestSEC026VelocityBurstRaisesOneSignalPerWindow`, `TestSEC026VelocityClockAtWindowBoundary` |
| Reciprocal signal changes no ledger entry | `TestSEC026ReciprocalPatternRaisesSignalWithoutLedgerChange` |
| Same-network administrators and reviewers only | `TestSEC026SignalsVisibleOnlyToSameNetworkReviewers`, API and page tests, route matrix |

Abuse cases also covered: concurrent proposals, failure not blocking the trade (mutation-checked), disabled policy, bounds, notice paging, erasure, database guards.

**Verification**
- Author run at `9d8adb1`: gofmt, vet and golangci-lint v2.15.0 clean (0 issues); `go test ./...` passes; race passes on service, store, api and web; hygiene and traceability pass.
- After merging #85 and current `main`, and renumbering: focused checks pass (SEC026, GOV021, migration, contract, OpenAPI, route-authz and catalogue tests across all packages), plus hygiene and traceability. The full local run is in progress; CI is authoritative.

**Owner decisions**

data.title: GOV-021: dual-approved administrator recovery for networks without an administrator
data.body:
Implements core requirement GOV-021 (P0, previously not built). Design record: `docs/audit/consolidation-completion-2026-11/GOV-021.md`. Operator runbook: `docs/ops/admin-recovery.md`.

**Flow**
- **Request.** An active member of a network that has no active administrator asks to be appointed. Only self-nomination is allowed.
  - Web: `/n/{slug}/admin-recovery` (CSRF, idempotency).
  - API: `POST /api/v1/admin-recovery/requests`. Accepts session cookies only, so a stolen API token cannot start an appointment.
  - If the network requires a second factor for administrators, the requester must have one.
- **Identity.** The signed-in account is checked against the network's recorded membership when the request is made, and again inside each approval's write.
- **Approval.** Operator CLI only: `circula admin-recovery list|approve|refuse`. Runs as the System actor, needs a reason, has no HTTP route (SEC-013 decision 4).
  - The first approval is only recorded.
  - A second approval under a different operator label applies the appointment, in one transaction with the state checks.
  - The same label (ignoring case and spacing) is refused, by the service and by the schema.
- **Effect.** The requester gets one ordinary admin role row and the "administrator required" state ends. No ledger table is touched (`TestGOV021RecoveryChangesNoBalanceOrEntry` compares digests and runs `VerifyLedger`).
- **Audit and notices.** Events are recorded at network and platform scope; members see each step without operator names or reasons. Every member receives a neutral notice at each step, including networks over 500 members.
- **Expiry.** Requests expire after 7 days (provisional).
- **Break-glass.** Kept separate: no break-glass session or grant is used. DEC-014 / A3-F02 stay open.

**Schema.** Migration `0019_admin_recovery.sql`: append-only, one transition per step; an applied row needs two distinct labels and the requester's own admin role row.

**API side effect.** Session-only network routes now resolve the network before the cookie-only check. Outsiders get not-found (API-017) instead of forbidden; members see no change.

**Coordination.** SEC-026, in progress on another branch, also adds a migration. Whichever merges second must rename its file to the next number (no code depends on the number) and regenerate traceability.

**Verification at `43d8e87`** (author run):
- gofmt clean, vet clean, golangci-lint v2.15.0 0 issues.
- `go test ./...` passes; hygiene and traceability pass.
- Race passes for store, api, web and cmd; `internal/service` passes alone with a 25-minute timeout (823 s).

After merging current `main` (#71, #72, #79) and resolving the `en.json` and traceability conflicts: hygiene and traceability pass; full unit and race runs are under way locally. This PR's CI is authoritative.

**Residual risks.** Operator identity is a typed label, because no operator accounts exist; one person typing two labels defeats dual approval, and only procedure and the member notices mitigate this. There is no objection period. Anyone with write access to the database file can bypass the service.

**Owner decisions needed:**
1. Authenticated operator identities.
2. A waiting or objection period before the second approval.
3. The 7-day expiry.
4. Whether a member may nominate another consenting member.

data.title: [owner decision] AUD4-F02: reviewer password resets only through the platform operator
data.body:
**Draft, policy pending. Do not merge without an owner decision.** This was split out of #82 at the independent consolidation review's request.

**Finding AUD4-F02 (Medium, CWE-284/639).** The SA2-01 guard stops a network administrator from resetting another administrator's password, but not a reviewer's.

An administrator who is a party to a dispute can therefore:
1. reset a reviewer who has no second factor;
2. sign in with the temporary password and set a new one;
3. decide their own dispute.

The audit probe produced the outcome "upheld" and moved the administrator's balance from -5000 to 0. This bypasses reviewer independence (DOM-038) for disputes and for GOV-016 challenges.

**What this candidate does.** It extends the operator-only reset rule to reviewers (`internal/service/recovery.go`). It adds the regression test `TestAdminCannotResetReviewerPassword`, which fails on `main` and passes with the change. Ordinary members can still be reset by administrators.

**Why it needs the owner:**
- It is a new recovery-policy choice. The SEC-008 addendum covers administrators and multi-network accounts. DOM-038 and SEC-010 require decision-party independence but do not choose this mechanism.
- On its own the guard is incomplete. An administrator can revoke the reviewer role, reset the now-ordinary account, and then regrant the role. This comes from reading the source, not from a test run.

**Options:**
- (a) Operator-only resets for reviewers, as here, plus a rule that covers revoke-and-regrant.
- (b) Require a second factor for reviewers.
- (c) Make a reviewer whose password was reset by an administrator ineligible to decide cases where that administrator is a party.

Details: `docs/audit/consolidation-completion-2026-11/AUD4-AUTH-FIXES.md` (in #82).
